document: Measured episode throughput on llm1 — for 8b budgeting (理 11433, idle slice)
method: read off the chains' OWN slice-completion timestamps from today's real arms. A line counts ONLY if it ends in 'episodes=<n>' — a '300/300' completion banner is not a slice, and counting it inflated the first version of this artifact by 30-50%.
for_8b: a v3-shaped 300-episode arm costs ~1.5 h on llm1 at budget 12, so an 8b generation (base + fit + wired arm) is a few hours of GPU rather than a day. The loop's cost is dominated by the NUMBER of generations, not by any single arm.
bounds: Wall clock on llm1 with nothing else on its GPU; today's llm2 work did not touch it.
BUDGET drives it — R5-C's 14-24 budgets are far slower per episode than budget 12.
SQL episodes are CHEAPER than v3's (4.3k vs 6.9k tokens/episode), so R7's rate is NOT the one to budget a v3-shaped 8b arm with. Use the R6 row.
No GPU was spent producing this: it is read off timestamps the chains already wrote.
